q: Warm-up 1. What does the suffix -ū indicate on a Perfect verb (e.g., ktabū)?
opts: The 3 f.sg. Perfect ends in -at (ketbat), not -ū.
explain: The Perfect is the suffix conjugation: person is marked at the end of the verb, and -ū is 3 m.pl.

q: Warm-up 2. Translate: Šbaq malkā l-ʾarʿā.
opts: In VSO order the noun right after the verb is the subject; l- marks the object.
Šbaq is Perfect (completed action), so English needs a past tense.
The king will leave the earth.
The future/Imperfect is not introduced until Lesson 8; šbaq is Perfect.

q: Warm-up 3. What happens to the vowels of k-t-b in the 3rd m.sg. Perfect?
opts: The vowel after the first radical drops (vowel reduction), giving ktab.
Right: Syriac reduces the short vowel in the open first syllable, so not *katab but ktab.
Katab is the Hebrew/Arabic shape; Syriac reduces the first vowel.
Prefixes belong to the Imperfect, not the Perfect.
The middle radical is doubled, giving kattab.
Doubling marks the Pael stem (Lesson 6), not the Peal Perfect.
explain: Vowel reduction is a hallmark of Syriac compared with Hebrew and Arabic.

q: Warm-up 4. Unvocalized ܟܬܒܬ can mean “I wrote” or “you (m) wrote.” How do you tell them apart?
opts: Only by context or vowel pointing.
Right: the consonants are identical (ketbet vs ktabt).
No extra letter is written; the spelling is the same.
w- means “and” and has nothing to do with person.
They cannot be told apart at all.
Readers rely on context, and vocalized texts mark the difference with points.
explain: Ambiguous consonantal forms are resolved by context or by vowel points.

q: Warm-up 5. Translate: w-qreb Yūḥannan.
opts: Qreb is a Perfect verb, not an adjective.
And they drew near to Yukhannan.

Exercise 3. Translate: ʾAbī ṭābā hū, w-ʾemī ṭābtā hī.
opts: My father is good, and my mother is good.
Right: verbless clauses with hū/hī as copula.
His father is good, and his mother is good.
My father is a king, and my mother is a queen.
My father was good, and my mother was good.
The pronoun copula gives a present “is.”

q: Exercise 3. Translate: Šbaqū talmīdē l-baythūn.
Exercise 3. Translate: Īt lān nūhrā rabbā.
opts: Right: literally “there is to us a great light.”
We do not have a great light.

q: Exercise 3. Translate: Qālā d-malkā b-ʾarʿan.
opts: The voice of the king is in our land.
The voice of the king is in his land.
The king’s word is in our land.
Our king’s voice is in the land.
The suffix is on ʾarʿā, not on malkā.

q: Exercise 4. Render into Syriac: “My brother is writing a word.”
opts: Ktab is Perfect “wrote”; “is writing” needs the participle.
Kātbā is the feminine participle; “brother” is masculine.

q: Exercise 4. “The king and his son are going to his kingdom.”
opts: Right: plural participle ʾāzlīn for a compound subject.
ʾEzal is Perfect “went”; “are going” needs the participle.
